To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose R-GCNs, a novel class of models for knowledge graph completion, and that they outperform the current state of the art.
we introduce R-GCNs, which are a generalization of Graph Convolutional Network to handle multi-relational data, and we demonstrate their usefulness in two knowledge base completion tasks.
R-GCNs: 1. are an effective stand-alone model for knowledge base entity classification, 2. improve link prediction performance of factorization models such as DistMult by a large margin.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (1) What kind of neural network architecture should be used for relational data, given the highly multi-relatinal nature of such data? and (2) Can a neural network architecture be used for knowledge base completion?
the following two problems: 1) how to learn a representation of the graph structure, and 2) how to use this representation for knowledge base completion.
the development of novel neural network architectures that can learn from and reason about the relational structure of knowledge bases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the R-GCN model is the most effective model for knowledge graph completion tasks.
R-GCNs can be used for knowledge graph reasoning and are a powerful tool for link prediction.
R-GCNs provide a simple, yet effective way to encode relational data and to leverage relational information in neural models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
R-GCN is a general model which can be used as a standalone model for classification task, as well as a decoder for link prediction task, and can achieve the state-of-art performance in both tasks.
we have proposed a novel model, namely Relational Graph Convolutinal Network (R-GCN) to model relational data, and have shown its effectiveness on knowledge base completion tasks.

we propose a novel neural network architecture, Relational Graph Convoltional Networks, for knowledge graphs, which can be used as a stand-alone encoder for entity classification, or as an encoder for a factorization model for link prediction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
R-GCNs can be used as a general-purpose encoder for relational data, which is applicable to a wide variety of tasks and models.
the relational structure inherent in knowledge bases is an important factor for modeling relational data and can be exploited to achieve state-of-the-art results.
R-GCNs provide a simple, powerful and flexible framework for knowledge graph reasoning.
